You are implementing Task 1.5: Imports, for the claude-md-optimizer rework (Phase 1).

## Task description

Read your task brief first: /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.5-brief.md
It gives the behaviour and test names. The controller's decisions below fill the gaps and override the brief where they differ.

## Context

Tasks 1.1 to 1.4 (done) built `claude-md-optimizer/scripts/claude_md/`: `limits.py`, `text.py`, `model.py` (`LoadedFile` with fields path, scope, mode, order, raw, text, paths, imported_by, external, notes; `Scope.IMPORT`), and `discovery.py` (`discover(project_dir, home_dir, managed_dir=None)` with a `_Loader` that assigns `order`, de-duplicates by resolved path and reads files via `_read`; it already discovers the CLAUDE.md family and rules). READ discovery.py, limits.py and the three discovery test files FIRST and extend in the same style. Before modifying any function, grep for its callers. This task extends `discovery.py` and `limits.py` and adds `tests/test_discovery_imports.py`. Do not modify the legacy script, `text.py` or `model.py`.

Working directory: /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer (git worktree, branch `fix/discovery-layer`). Work only here. Never touch /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer outside this worktree; never use `git -C`; do not `cd` into subdirectories. Run Python with `uv run`.

## Decisions from the controller

Step 1 of the brief (verify the max import depth in the docs) is DONE by the controller. Anthropic's memory docs state: "Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops", "Both relative and absolute paths are allowed. Relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory", imports of `~/...` are allowed, and an import is "external when its path resolves outside your working directory" (Claude Code then asks the user to approve it; user-scope files such as `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.claude/rules/` load their imports without the dialog). So:
- In `limits.py` change `MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH` to `Limit(4, True, <the memory docs URL constant already used>)` and update `tests/test_limits.py` (it currently asserts this limit is unverified with value 5; keep `COMBINED_LINES` unverified).
- Hops: the importing file is depth 0. Its direct imports are hop 1, their imports hop 2, and so on. Files at hops 1 to 4 are loaded; an import found in a hop-4 file is NOT expanded and the hop-4 file gets the note `"import depth limit reached: <token>"`.

Which files expand imports: files with `LoadMode.ALWAYS` in scopes MANAGED, USER, USER_RULE, ANCESTOR, PROJECT, LOCAL, PROJECT_RULE, and (recursively) IMPORT. NOT conditional rules, NOT nested/on-demand files, NOT SKIPPED files.

Syntax: an import is a token starting with `@` that is preceded by whitespace or the start of a line (so `user@example.com` is NOT an import), followed by non-whitespace path characters. Strip trailing punctuation (one or more of `.,;:!?)]}'"` ) from the token before resolving; if the token with its punctuation intact resolves to an existing file prefer that. Ignore any `@` inside fenced code blocks (``` or ~~~) and inside inline code spans (single or multiple backticks). Use the same fence logic as `claude_md.text.strip_html_comments` if it exposes a reusable helper; otherwise a small helper in discovery.py is fine (do not modify text.py).

Resolution: `~` or `~/...` resolves against the `home_dir` argument (never the real home); absolute paths as given; anything else relative to the directory of the file containing the import. Resolve symlinks for dedup (the loader already dedups by resolved path; an already-loaded file is not loaded twice, and a file imported twice yields one entry).

Result entries: scope `Scope.IMPORT`, mode `LoadMode.ALWAYS`, `imported_by` = the path of the file containing the import, `raw` and `text` via the shared read helper with `effective_text(raw, is_rule=False)` (BOM, invalid UTF-8 note, 4 MiB skip, unreadable skip all apply). Placement: depth-first, each imported file immediately after its importer, in order of appearance. `external=True` when the importer is project-level (scopes PROJECT, ANCESTOR, LOCAL, PROJECT_RULE, or an IMPORT whose chain started at one of those) AND the resolved import path is not inside `project_dir`; always False for imports found in MANAGED, USER or USER_RULE files and their chains.

Notes (appended to the IMPORTING file's `notes`): a token that looks like a path (contains `/` or ends with an extension such as `.md`) but whose target does not exist gets `"import target missing: <token>"`; a token that does not look like a path and does not exist (for example `@mention`) is ignored silently. A cycle (an import that resolves to a file already on the current import chain) is not loaded again and the importing file gets `"circular import: <token>"`; this must terminate. A directory target is treated as missing.

Tests (`tests/test_discovery_imports.py`): the six in the brief (`test_import_counts_as_own_file`, `test_nested_imports_expand`, `test_circular_import_terminates_and_notes`, `test_external_import_flagged`, `test_import_in_code_block_ignored`, `test_missing_import_target_is_noted`) plus: relative import resolves from the importing file's directory (an import inside a nested `docs/a.md` of `@b.md` finds `docs/b.md`); `~` uses the passed home_dir; absolute path; the fifth hop is not loaded and the hop-4 file has the depth note (build a chain of six files); inline code span ignored; email address not an import; trailing punctuation stripped (`see @docs/x.md.`); import from a USER file outside the project has `external=False`, the same from a project file has `external=True`; a conditional rule's imports are not expanded; an imported file also reachable as a normal file appears once; the imported file's order immediately follows its importer; `@mention` ignored silently; imports expanded for an unconditional rule; an imported file larger than 4 MiB is SKIPPED. Filter results to files under tmp_path and assert on scope, mode, order, imported_by, external and notes.

## Rules

- TDD: write the failing tests first, run them (`uv run pytest tests/test_discovery_imports.py tests/test_limits.py -v`), watch them fail for the right reason, implement, run again. Put RED and GREEN evidence in the report.
- Run `uv run pytest -v`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .` before committing; all must pass (3 xfailed expected; existing tests must still pass).
- Code comments only where necessary. Prefer none.
- Git: `git branch --show-current` first (must be `fix/discovery-layer`). Stage by explicit path (discovery.py, limits.py, tests/test_limits.py, tests/test_discovery_imports.py, plus any other file you had to change), never `git add -A` or `git add .`. Never skip hooks. One git command per call.
- Commit message: `feat: expand @imports`, a blank line, then `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- You do not dispatch subagents.

## Report

Write your full report to /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.5-report.md: what you implemented, test results, TDD evidence, files changed, self-review findings, concerns.

Then reply with ONLY (under 15 lines): Status (DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT), commits (short SHA + subject), a one-line test summary, concerns, report path.

You are reviewing one task's implementation: first whether it matches its requirements, then whether it is well-built. This is a task-scoped gate, not a merge review.

## What Was Requested

Read the task brief: /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.5-brief.md

Global constraints (verbatim from the plan): runtime is standard-library Python 3.13; pytest and ruff via uv. Docs-backed behaviour carries a source URL; unconfirmed facts are labelled "unverified". Never skip pre-commit hooks; stage by explicit path; commits end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

Anthropic's documented behaviour (Claude Code memory docs, "Import additional files"): CLAUDE.md files can import additional files with `@path/to/import`; imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch alongside the CLAUDE.md that references them; both relative and absolute paths are allowed; relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory; imported files can recursively import other files, "with a maximum depth of four hops"; an import in a project-level memory file is "external when its path resolves outside your working directory" and Claude Code asks the user to approve it; user-scope files (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/rules/`) load their imports without the dialog. `~/...` paths are allowed.

Controller decisions that fill gaps (check the diff against them):
- `limits.py`: `MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH = Limit(4, True, <memory docs URL>)` (was unverified 5); `tests/test_limits.py` updated; `COMBINED_LINES` stays unverified.
- Hops: the importing file is depth 0; its direct imports are hop 1, and so on. Hops 1 to 4 are loaded; an import found in a hop-4 file is NOT expanded and that file gets the note `"import depth limit reached: <token>"`.
- Which files expand imports: `LoadMode.ALWAYS` files in scopes MANAGED, USER, USER_RULE, ANCESTOR, PROJECT, LOCAL, PROJECT_RULE and (recursively) IMPORT. NOT conditional rules, NOT nested/on-demand files, NOT SKIPPED files.
- Syntax: a token starting with `@`, preceded by whitespace or start of line (so `user@example.com` is not an import), followed by non-whitespace path characters; trailing punctuation (`.,;:!?)]}'"`) stripped before resolving, preferring the unstripped token if it resolves; `@` inside fenced code blocks and inline code spans (single or multiple backticks) ignored.
- Resolution: `~` / `~/...` against the `home_dir` argument (never the real home); absolute as given; otherwise relative to the importing file's directory. Dedup by resolved path (a file imported twice, or also reachable as a normal file, appears once).
- Entries: scope IMPORT, mode ALWAYS, `imported_by` = importing file's path, text via `effective_text(raw, is_rule=False)`; BOM, invalid UTF-8 note, 4 MiB skip and unreadable skip apply. Placement: depth-first, each imported file immediately after its importer, in order of appearance. `external=True` only when the importer is project-level (PROJECT, ANCESTOR, LOCAL, PROJECT_RULE, or an IMPORT whose chain started at one of those) AND the resolved path is not inside `project_dir`; always False for chains rooted in MANAGED, USER, USER_RULE.
- Notes go on the IMPORTING file: path-looking token (contains `/` or ends with an extension) that does not exist: `"import target missing: <token>"`; non-path-looking nonexistent token (e.g. `@mention`) ignored silently; a cycle (import resolving to a file already on the current chain) is not loaded again and the importer gets `"circular import: <token>"`; a directory target counts as missing.

**Base:** 760c968  **Head:** d6ea6f2
**Diff file:** /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.5-review-package.md

You MAY run focused Python checks with `PYTHONPATH=claude-md-optimizer/scripts uv run python -c "..."` using temporary directories you create under the system temp dir (create no files in the repo), and `uv run pytest tests/test_discovery_imports.py tests/test_limits.py -q`. Name each check. Your review is read-only on the repo. Do not dispatch subagents.

## Named risks to check by EXECUTION

1. Hop boundary: build a chain root -> f1 -> f2 -> f3 -> f4 -> f5 -> f6 (each importing the next). Print which are loaded and which file carries the depth note. Exactly f1..f4 must load; f4 carries the note; f5, f6 absent. Also check the boundary when the chain is reached via a CLAUDE.local.md and via an unconditional rule.
2. Cycle on the chain vs diamond: A imports B and C; B imports D; C imports D. D must load once (diamond, not a cycle) and the second importer must NOT get a "circular import" note. Then a true cycle A -> B -> A: terminates; which file gets the note.
3. Syntax: `@docs/x.md.`, `(see @docs/x.md)`, `"@docs/x.md"`, `- @docs/x.md`, `# @docs/x.md` (heading), `@docs/x.md,@docs/y.md` (two on one token), `@docs/x.md#section`, a Windows-style `@docs\x.md`, an `@` inside a markdown link `[a](@docs/x.md)`, a double-backtick code span containing `@docs/x.md`, an indented (4 spaces) code block containing an import (CommonMark indented code, not fenced), and an unterminated fence. For each state whether it loads and whether that is reasonable given the documented behaviour; flag anything that creates a spurious import or misses an obvious one.
4. External flag: project file importing `../outside.md` and `~/x.md`; USER file importing `../x.md`; an import chain project -> inside -> outside (the outside one external?); an ancestor file importing a file in project_dir.
5. Interaction: an imported file that is also an unconditional rule; an imported file listed in `claudeMdExcludes`-like context is out of scope; imported file with frontmatter or HTML comments (text stripped as non-rule?); imported file larger than 4 MiB; an import path with spaces; an import pointing at a symlink loop.
6. Performance: 300 files each importing 5 others (fan-out) and a 4-hop chain with 50 imports per file: time it; no exponential blow-up.
7. Test quality: real behaviour, not vacuous; independence from unrelated real files in tmp_path's ancestors.

## Part 1: Spec Compliance
Missing / Extra / Misunderstood against the brief, the decisions and the documented behaviour. Verify every test name in the brief exists and `limits.py`/`test_limits.py` were updated as decided.

## Part 2: Code Quality
Extends existing style, no duplicated reading logic, helper size, naming, comments only where needed. Cite file:line for every finding.

Your final message is the report itself, starting directly with the spec-compliance verdict.

## Calibration
Important means the task cannot be trusted until fixed (wrong hop count, spurious or missed import for a documented form, wrong external flag, a false "circular" note on a diamond, a hang, vacuous tests). Polish is Minor. Acknowledge what was done well first.

### Spec Compliance
- ✅ Spec compliant | ❌ Issues found: [file:line]
- ⚠️ Cannot verify from diff: [items]

### Strengths

### Issues
#### Critical (Must Fix)
#### Important (Should Fix)
#### Minor (Nice to Have)

### Assessment
**Task quality:** Approved | Needs fixes
**Reasoning:** 1-2 sentences.

The bug is real: if a file is first reached at the depth limit and later reached at a shallower hop, its imports are never expanded. input.message:
Review of Task 1.5 found one Important issue (fix round 1 of 5). Scope: discovery.py (the import expansion code) and tests/test_discovery_imports.py only.

FINDING (reviewer, verified by execution): Dedup makes the hop limit order-dependent (discovery.py:99-100). If a file is first loaded at hop 4 and left unexpanded, a later shallower import of it hits `key in self._seen` and `continue`, so its children are never expanded. With `CLAUDE.md = "@f1.md\n@f4.md"` and the chain f1 -> f2 -> f3 -> f4 -> f5 -> f6, the result was f1..f4 only, and f4 keeps `import depth limit reached: @f5.md`, although f4 is also a direct hop-1 import whose children (f5, f6) should load. The loaded set must not depend on the order in which imports appear.

Required behaviour:
- Track, per resolved import path, the smallest hop at which it has been reached (and whether its imports were expanded). When an already-loaded import is reached again at a SMALLER hop than before and its earlier expansion was cut short by the depth limit, expand its imports now at the new hop. Do not add the file itself a second time (still one entry per file). Newly discovered children are appended at the current end of the load order (they cannot be placed retroactively after the file; keep `order` contiguous and strictly increasing).
- When that re-expansion happens, the `import depth limit reached: ...` note on that file must no longer be present if its imports are now fully expanded (remove it; if some of its children are still cut off at the new hop, the note for the still-cut tokens may remain). Cycle detection and diamond handling must be unchanged: a diamond still loads once with no circular note, and a true cycle still terminates with its note.
- Re-expansion must terminate and must not blow up on large fan-outs (keep the performance profile: the earlier review measured 300 files x 5 imports in 0.045 s and a 4-hop 50-wide tree in 0.15 s; stay in that range).

Tests to add: (1) `CLAUDE.md = "@f1.md\n@f4.md"` with chain f1..f6: all of f1..f6 are loaded, f4 has no depth note, each file appears once; (2) the same files with the lines reversed (`"@f4.md\n@f1.md"`): the same SET of loaded files; (3) a file reached first at hop 1 and later at hop 4 is not re-expanded or duplicated, and its children are not duplicated; (4) the existing cycle and diamond tests still pass unchanged. Keep every existing test passing.

Rules: TDD (write the failing tests, run them and record RED, then implement and record GREEN). Run `uv run pytest -v`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`. You are re-reviewing one task's fix round. A previous review produced a finding; an implementer has attempted to fix it. Verdict the finding and inspect the fix diff for new breakage. Nothing else.

## The Task

Read the task brief: /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.5-brief.md. Behaviour modelled (Claude Code memory docs): CLAUDE.md files import files with `@path`; imports are recursive with a maximum depth of four hops. In this implementation the importing file is depth 0, its direct imports are hop 1, and so on; hops 1 to 4 load; an import found in a hop-4 file is not expanded and that file gets the note `"import depth limit reached: <token>"`. Diamond imports load once with no circular note; a true cycle terminates and the file doing the back-import gets `"circular import: <token>"`.

## The Finding Under Verification

Dedup makes the hop limit order-dependent (discovery.py:99-100). If a file is first loaded at hop 4 and left unexpanded, a later shallower import of it hit `key in self._seen` and `continue`, so its children were never expanded. With `CLAUDE.md = "@f1.md\n@f4.md"` and the chain f1 -> f2 -> f3 -> f4 -> f5 -> f6, the result was f1..f4 only, and f4 kept `import depth limit reached: @f5.md`, although f4 is also a direct hop-1 import whose children (f5, f6) should load. The loaded set must not depend on the order in which imports appear.

Required fix behaviour: track per resolved import path the smallest hop reached and whether its imports were expanded; when a depth-cut import is reached again at a strictly smaller hop, expand its imports then (the file itself is not added twice); newly discovered children append at the current end of the load order (keep `order` contiguous and increasing); the stale depth note is removed when its imports are now fully expanded; cycle and diamond handling unchanged; terminates and no performance blow-up (earlier measurements: 300 files x 5 imports in 0.045 s; a 4-hop tree with 50 imports per file in 0.15 s).

## The Fix

Read the diff file once. Do not re-run git commands. You MAY run focused Python checks with `PYTHONPATH=claude-md-optimizer/scripts uv run python -c "..."` (temp dirs under the system temp dir only; create no files in the repo) and `uv run pytest tests/test_discovery_imports.py -q`. Name each check. Your review is read-only. Do not dispatch subagents.

## What to verify (execute, don't just read)

1. The reported failing case: `@f1.md` then `@f4.md` with chain f1..f6: loaded set is f1..f6, f4 has no depth note, each file once. Reverse the two lines: the same set. Print `order` values and confirm they are contiguous and strictly increasing, and `imported_by` for f5 and f6.
2. Order independence generally: generate a root with 3-5 imports to files at various positions of a deep chain (f1..f8) in all permutations (at most 24); the SET of loaded files must be identical across permutations. Report any difference.
3. A file reached first at a shallow hop and later at a deeper hop: not re-expanded, not duplicated, children not duplicated.
4. Diamond (A imports B and C; B and C import D) and true cycle (A -> B -> A) behave as before, including notes (no circular note on a diamond).
5. Depth-note hygiene: after re-expansion, f4 has no `import depth limit reached` note; if some children remain cut off at the new hop, what does the note say? Construct a case (chain of 8, root imports f1 and f4) and report notes on every file.
6. Performance: re-time 300 files each importing 5 others, and a 4-hop tree with 50 imports per file, and a worst-case for re-expansion (many files first reached deep then shallow). Report timings; flag anything over 1 second.
7. Whole test module passes; the new tests would have failed on the old code (judge from the removed lines).

The re-review is right, and the verdict stands: **NOT ADDRESSED**. The reported case is fixed, but the underlying bug, order-dependence, is still there in a neighbouring form. Four of eight tested import selections still produced different loaded sets depending on order. The repro: `@f1.md` then `@f3.md` loads f1..f4, but the reverse order loads f1..f6. My earlier fix patched one symptom; the real defect is that the code doesn't compute a true minimum-hop reachability.

The robust design is a "relaxation" rule: record the smallest hop at which each file has been reached, and re-expand a file's imports whenever it's reached at a strictly *smaller* hop, whether or not it was itself cut. Since hops are bounded at 4, that terminates quickly. This is fix round 2 of 5, and I'm asking for a property test against an independent oracle, so the next version can't pass by luck.

input.message:
The scoped re-review of fix round 1 found the finding NOT ADDRESSED (fix round 2 of 5). Scope: discovery.py (import expansion) and tests/test_discovery_imports.py only.

FINDING (reviewer, verified by execution): the loaded set still depends on import order when a shallower reach hits a file that is NOT itself depth-cut but has a depth-cut descendant. Minimal repro, chain f1 -> f2 -> ... -> f8: root `@f1.md` then `@f3.md` loads f1..f4 only (f4 keeps `import depth limit reached: @f5.md`); root `@f3.md` then `@f1.md` loads f1..f6. Cause: `_reexpand` returns early when `key not in self._cut` (discovery.py:108). f3 was loaded at hop 3 and was not cut; its child f4 was cut at hop 4; when f3 is reached again at hop 1 nothing happens, so f4 is never revisited at hop 2. Across all permutations of the root's imports on a chain of 8, four selections gave more than one distinct loaded set: (1,3,5), (2,4,6), (1,2,3,4), (3,4,5,6). Selections (2,5,7), (1,4,6,8), (3,5,7), (2,3,5,7,8) were stable.

Please replace the patched special-casing with a correct and simple rule (relaxation of the minimum hop):
- Keep, per resolved import path, `best_hop` = the smallest hop at which it has been reached so far.
- When an import resolves at hop h: if the path has never been seen, add it (one entry, as now), set `best_hop = h`, and expand its imports at hop h+1 if h < MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH.value, otherwise note the cut. If the path was seen and h < best_hop, set `best_hop = h` and expand ITS imports again at hop h+1 (each child applies the same rule recursively, so descendants are relaxed too, whether or not the file itself was ever cut). If h >= best_hop, do nothing. Since hops are bounded and strictly decrease, this terminates and does at most MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH relaxations per file.
- Cycle detection stays chain-based as now (an import that resolves to a file on the current import chain is not loaded again and the importer gets `circular import: <token>`), and diamonds still load once with no circular note.
- Depth notes must reflect the FINAL state: a file's `import depth limit reached: <token>` note exists only if, at its final `best_hop`, it is at the depth limit and has that import; remove stale notes when a file is relaxed to a smaller hop (re-expansion may then add the note to a deeper descendant instead). Make sure the notes are deterministic regardless of import order (same notes for the same set of files).
- Newly reached files always append at the current end of the load order (keep `order` contiguous and strictly increasing). The ORDER of files may differ between permutations; the SET of loaded files and the NOTES must not.

Tests to add (keep all existing tests passing):
1. A property-style test with an INDEPENDENT oracle: build chain f1..f8 (fk imports f(k+1)), and for each of these root import selections (1,3,5), (2,4,6), (1,2,3,4), (3,4,5,6), (2,5,7), (3,5,7), (2,3,5,7,8), take ALL permutations of the root's import lines (at most 24 each) and assert (a) the set of loaded import files equals the set predicted by a simple breadth-first search written in the test (a file is loaded if its minimum hop from the root, counting each direct import as hop 1, is <= 4), (b) the set of (file, note) pairs is the same for every permutation, (c) each file appears exactly once, (d) `order` values are contiguous and strictly increasing.
2. The explicit minimal repro in both orders (`@f1.md`,`@f3.md` and reverse): both load f1..f7... compute the expected set with the oracle rather than hard-coding it by hand, and also assert it explicitly for this case.
3. The earlier regression tests (the `@f1.md`/`@f4.md` pair, shallow-then-deep not re-expanded or duplicated, diamond, true cycle) still pass unchanged.

Rules: TDD (write the failing tests first and record RED, then implement and record GREEN). Run `uv run pytest -v`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`. Re-time two cases and put the numbers in the report: 300 files each importing 5 others, and a 4-hop tree with 50 imports per file (earlier: 0.02 s and 0.19 s); they must stay under 1 s. Commit as a NEW commit after `git branch --show-current` shows fix/discovery-layer; stage by explicit path; message `fix: relax import hops so the loaded set is order-independent`, a blank line, then `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Append a fix report to /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.5-report.md. toolu_01EzshSXEKavGCPpS5bYmH7Y.message:
The scoped re-review of fix round 1 found the finding NOT ADDRESSED (fix round 2 of 5). Scope: discovery.py (import expansion) and tests/test_discovery_imports.py only.

FINDING (reviewer, verified by execution): the loaded set still depends on import order when a shallower reach hits a file that is NOT itself depth-cut but has a depth-cut descendant. Minimal repro, chain f1 -> f2 -> ... -> f8: root `@f1.md` then `@f3.md` loads f1..f4 only (f4 keeps `import depth limit reached: @f5.md`); root `@f3.md` then `@f1.md` loads f1..f6. Cause: `_reexpand` returns early when `key not in self._cut` (discovery.py:108). f3 was loaded at hop 3 and was not cut; its child f4 was cut at hop 4; when f3 is reached again at hop 1 nothing happens, so f4 is never revisited at hop 2. Across all permutations of the root's imports on a chain of 8, four selections gave more than one distinct loaded set: (1,3,5), (2,4,6), (1,2,3,4), (3,4,5,6). Selections (2,5,7), (1,4,6,8), (3,5,7), (2,3,5,7,8) were stable.

Please replace the patched special-casing with a correct and simple rule (relaxation of the minimum hop):
- Keep, per resolved import path, `best_hop` = the smallest hop at which it has been reached so far.
- When an import resolves at hop h: if the path has never been seen, add it (one entry, as now), set `best_hop = h`, and expand its imports at hop h+1 if h < MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH.value, otherwise note the cut. If the path was seen and h < best_hop, set `best_hop = h` and expand ITS imports again at hop h+1 (each child applies the same rule recursively, so descendants are relaxed too, whether or not the file itself was ever cut). If h >= best_hop, do nothing. Since hops are bounded and strictly decrease, this terminates and does at most MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH relaxations per file.
- Cycle detection stays chain-based as now (an import that resolves to a file on the current import chain is not loaded again and the importer gets `circular import: <token>`), and diamonds still load once with no circular note.
- Depth notes must reflect the FINAL state: a file's `import depth limit reached: <token>` note exists only if, at its final `best_hop`, it is at the depth limit and has that import; remove stale notes when a file is relaxed to a smaller hop (re-expansion may then add the note to a deeper descendant instead). Make sure the notes are deterministic regardless of import order (same notes for the same set of files).
- Newly reached files always append at the current end of the load order (keep `order` contiguous and strictly increasing). The ORDER of files may differ between permutations; the SET of loaded files and the NOTES must not.

Tests to add (keep all existing tests passing):
1. A property-style test with an INDEPENDENT oracle: build chain f1..f8 (fk imports f(k+1)), and for each of these root import selections (1,3,5), (2,4,6), (1,2,3,4), (3,4,5,6), (2,5,7), (3,5,7), (2,3,5,7,8), take ALL permutations of the root's import lines (at most 24 each) and assert (a) the set of loaded import files equals the set predicted by a simple breadth-first search written in the test (a file is loaded if its minimum hop from the root, counting each direct import as hop 1, is <= 4), (b) the set of (file, note) pairs is the same for every permutation, (c) each file appears exactly once, (d) `order` values are contiguous and strictly increasing.
2. The explicit minimal repro in both orders (`@f1.md`,`@f3.md` and reverse): both load f1..f7... compute the expected set with the oracle rather than hard-coding it by hand, and also assert it explicitly for this case.
3. The earlier regression tests (the `@f1.md`/`@f4.md` pair, shallow-then-deep not re-expanded or duplicated, diamond, true cycle) still pass unchanged.

Rules: TDD (write the failing tests first and record RED, then implement and record GREEN). Run `uv run pytest -v`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`. Re-time two cases and put the numbers in the report: 300 files each importing 5 others, and a 4-hop tree with 50 imports per file (earlier: 0.02 s and 0.19 s); they must stay under 1 s. You are re-reviewing one task's second fix round. Verdict the open finding and inspect the fix diff for new breakage. Nothing else.

## The Task

Task brief: /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.5-brief.md. Behaviour modelled (Claude Code memory docs): `@path` imports are recursive with a maximum depth of four hops. In this implementation the importing file is depth 0, direct imports are hop 1; files at hops 1 to 4 load; an import found in a hop-4 file is not expanded and that file gets the note `"import depth limit reached: <token>"`. Diamonds load once with no circular note; a cycle terminates and the file doing the back-import gets `"circular import: <token>"`.

## The Open Finding

The loaded set of import files must NOT depend on the order in which imports appear. The previous fix handled `@f1.md` then `@f4.md` but not a shallow reach of a non-cut file with a depth-cut descendant: on chain f1->f2->...->f8, root `@f1.md` then `@f3.md` loaded f1..f4 only, while `@f3.md` then `@f1.md` loaded f1..f6. Four of eight root selections ((1,3,5), (2,4,6), (1,2,3,4), (3,4,5,6)) gave more than one distinct set across permutations.

The implementer's second fix is a minimum-hop relaxation: each import keeps its smallest hop; a file reached again at a strictly smaller hop has its imports expanded again (descendants relax recursively); depth-limit notes are recomputed whenever a file is expanded so they depend only on final hops; cycle detection stays chain-based; new files append at the end of the load order (order contiguous, strictly increasing).

## The Fix

Implementer's report (fix round 2 at the end): /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.5-report.md

Name each check. Your review is read-only. Do not dispatch subagents.

1. Write YOUR OWN oracle and fuzz it (the implementer's tests share the implementer's assumptions): generate at least 300 random import graphs (6 to 10 files, each file importing 0 to 4 random others, including self-imports, back-edges and diamonds) with a random root that imports 1 to 5 of them; for each graph try at least 6 random permutations of the root's import lines AND random permutations of the import lines inside each file. Compute the expected loaded set with a plain breadth-first search (a file is loaded iff its minimum hop from the root is <= 4, a direct import being hop 1). Assert the implementation's set of loaded import files equals the oracle's, in every trial. Report the number of trials and any mismatch with a minimal repro.
2. Notes across permutations: for the same graphs, compare the set of (file, note) pairs for the `import depth limit reached` and `circular import` notes across permutations. Depth notes should depend only on final hops. Circular-import notes are inherently chain-based: report whether they vary with order, give a minimal repro, and judge whether that variation matters (it is acceptable for a circular note to appear on a different file in a different order as long as the LOADED SET is stable; say so explicitly either way).
3. Termination and counts: confirm each file appears at most once, `order` is contiguous and strictly increasing, and no trial hangs (use a per-trial time limit of 5 seconds).
4. Re-expansion cost: time (a) 300 files each importing 5 others, (b) a layered graph of 4 layers x 50 files where every file imports all 50 files of the next layer, (c) the worst case for relaxation you can construct (many files first reached at hop 4, then reached at hop 1 in reverse order). Report timings and flag anything over 1 second.
5. Regression: diamond (A imports B, C; both import D) loads D once with no circular note; true cycle A->B->A terminates and B gets `circular import: @A.md`; a self-import terminates; the hop-4 boundary on a chain of 6 loads f1..f4 with the note on f4.
6. The new tests would have failed on the old code (judge from the removed lines) and are not vacuous.

Your final message is the report itself, starting directly with the verdict.

ADDRESSED | NOT ADDRESSED, with the fuzz results (trials, mismatches).

With severity and file:line, or "None".

Which new tests would fail on the old code.

### Out-of-Scope Observations
Non-blocking, or "None".

### Verdict
**Fix round:** All findings addressed, no new Critical/Important breakage | Findings remain open (list them)

You are implementing Task 1.6: AGENTS.md and claudeMdExcludes, for the claude-md-optimizer rework (Phase 1).

## Task description

Read your task brief first: /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.6-brief.md

## Context

Tasks 1.1 to 1.5 (done) built `claude-md-optimizer/scripts/claude_md/`: `limits.py`, `text.py`, `model.py` (`LoadedFile`; `Scope.AGENTS`; `LoadMode` incl. `ALWAYS`, `ON_DEMAND`, `EXCLUDED`, `DORMANT`), and `discovery.py` (`discover(project_dir, home_dir, managed_dir=None)`; a `_Loader` that assigns `order`, de-duplicates by resolved path, reads files, expands `@imports` with min-hop relaxation; it discovers the CLAUDE.md family, rules, nested CLAUDE.md files and imports). READ discovery.py and its four test files FIRST and extend in the same style; the import code is delicate (an independent fuzz verified order-independence), so do not change its behaviour. Before modifying any function, grep for its callers. This task extends `discovery.py` and adds `tests/test_discovery_agents_excludes.py`. Do not modify the legacy script, `text.py`, `model.py` or `limits.py`.

Working directory: /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer (git worktree, branch `fix/discovery-layer`). Work only here. Never touch /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer outside this worktree; never use `git -C`; do not `cd` into subdirectories. Run Python with `uv run`.

## What Anthropic's docs say (Claude Code memory docs; implement exactly this)

AGENTS.md: "By default, Claude reads AGENTS.md only when you have no CLAUDE.md in your working directory or above it." These count (so AGENTS.md is NOT read): a `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` in the working directory or any directory above it. These do NOT count: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, the managed CLAUDE.md, and `.claude/rules/` files. When none count: at session start Claude reads every `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/AGENTS.md` in the working directory and the directories above it; as Claude works in subdirectories, a subdirectory's `AGENTS.md` loads when Claude opens a file there AND that subdirectory has none of the three CLAUDE.md files of its own. `@path` imports inside an AGENTS.md are expanded. NOT read: `AGENTS.local.md`, `AGENTS.override.md`, anything under a `.agents/` directory.

claudeMdExcludes: a setting, valid in any settings layer (user, project, local, managed); an array of glob patterns matched against ABSOLUTE file paths; arrays merge across layers; example `["**/monorepo/CLAUDE.md", "/home/user/monorepo/other-team/.claude/rules/**"]`; a managed CLAUDE.md cannot be excluded by individual settings.

## Decisions from the controller

AGENTS.md:
- Compute `has_claude`: true if, for any directory D from the filesystem root down to `project_dir`, `D/CLAUDE.md`, `D/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `D/CLAUDE.local.md` exists (existence only; ancestor `.claude/CLAUDE.md` counts here even though the existing code does not LOAD it; this is ruling R17, leave that as is). Do not count the user, managed or rules files.
- If `has_claude` is false: for each directory D from the filesystem root down to `project_dir`, `D/AGENTS.md` then `D/.claude/AGENTS.md` become `Scope.AGENTS`, `LoadMode.ALWAYS`, read through the same helper (BOM, invalid UTF-8, 4 MiB, unreadable), `text = effective_text(raw, is_rule=False)`, placed in load order at the point where that directory's CLAUDE.md files would sit (before that directory's `CLAUDE.local.md` slot, which cannot exist when `has_claude` is false), and their `@imports` are expanded like any other always-on file (add `Scope.AGENTS` to the scopes that expand imports). Nested AGENTS.md: every `AGENTS.md` in a subdirectory strictly below `project_dir` whose own directory contains none of `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md` becomes `Scope.AGENTS`, `LoadMode.ON_DEMAND`, ordered after all other files (use the same walk and pruning as nested CLAUDE.md).
- If `has_claude` is true: any `AGENTS.md` / `.claude/AGENTS.md` in the directory chain is returned as `Scope.AGENTS`, `LoadMode.DORMANT` (raw/text read normally so the report can show it, note `"AGENTS.md not loaded: a CLAUDE.md exists at or above the working directory"`). Do not return nested AGENTS.md files in this case.
- Never read `AGENTS.local.md`, `AGENTS.override.md` or `.agents/`.
- The `/config` "Project instructions" setting is NOT read (ruling R18); do not try.

claudeMdExcludes:
- Read `claudeMdExcludes` from these four files if they exist: `home_dir/.claude/settings.json`, `home_dir/.claude/settings.local.json`, `project_dir/.claude/settings.json`, `project_dir/.claude/settings.local.json`. Merge arrays (concatenate, keep order, drop duplicates). Ignore a file that is unreadable, not valid JSON, not an object, or whose `claudeMdExcludes` is not a list; ignore non-string entries. Never raise.
- Matching: a pattern starting with `~/` expands against the `home_dir` argument; match each file's absolute resolved path with `PurePath.full_match` (Python 3.13) against the pattern; also try the file's unresolved absolute path (so a pattern written against a symlinked location still matches).
- Effect: a matching file (any scope EXCEPT `Scope.MANAGED`) gets `LoadMode.EXCLUDED` and the note `"excluded by claudeMdExcludes: <pattern>"` (first matching pattern); keep its raw/text. Exclusion is decided when the file is added, BEFORE imports are expanded, so an excluded file's imports are not loaded. A managed CLAUDE.md is never excluded. Excluded files count nowhere in totals (existing behaviour of `totals`).
- Tests: the seven in the brief (`test_agents_loaded_when_no_claude_md`, `test_agents_dormant_when_claude_md_exists`, `test_claude_local_md_counts_as_claude_md`, `test_user_claude_md_does_not_suppress_agents`, `test_excludes_glob_marks_file`, `test_excludes_merge_across_settings`, `test_unreadable_settings_json_is_ignored`) plus: `.claude/AGENTS.md` read; an ancestor `AGENTS.md` loaded when no CLAUDE.md anywhere; an ancestor `.claude/CLAUDE.md` suppresses AGENTS (R17) while still not being loaded itself; `.claude/rules` file and managed CLAUDE.md do not suppress; nested AGENTS.md ON_DEMAND only when its directory has no CLAUDE.md family file; nested AGENTS ignored when dormant; `AGENTS.local.md`/`AGENTS.override.md`/`.agents/` never read; imports inside a loaded AGENTS.md are expanded; managed CLAUDE.md is not excluded even if a pattern matches; an excluded file's imports are not loaded; a `~/` pattern; the example pattern shapes `**/x/CLAUDE.md` and `<abs>/.claude/rules/**`; settings file that is a JSON list, or has a non-list `claudeMdExcludes`, or non-string entries; duplicates across layers collapse; excluded rules and excluded AGENTS files get EXCLUDED. Filter results to files under tmp_path and assert on scope, mode, order and notes.

## Rules

- TDD: write the failing tests first, run them (`uv run pytest tests/test_discovery_agents_excludes.py -v`), watch them fail for the right reason, implement, run again. Put RED and GREEN evidence in the report.
- Run `uv run pytest -v`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .` before committing; all must pass (3 xfailed expected; ALL existing tests must still pass, in particular the import tests).
- Code comments only where necessary. Prefer none.
- Git: `git branch --show-current` first (must be `fix/discovery-layer`). Stage by explicit path, never `git add -A` or `git add .`. Never skip hooks. One git command per call.
- Commit message: `feat: model AGENTS.md and claudeMdExcludes`, a blank line, then `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- You do not dispatch subagents.

## Report

Write your full report to /Users/rod/build/claude-md-optimizer/.claude/worktrees/fix+discovery-layer/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-02-claude-md-optimizer-rework/task-1.6-report.md: what you implemented, test results, TDD evidence, files changed, self-review findings, concerns (including behaviours you were unsure about).

Then reply with ONLY (under 15 lines): Status (DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT), commits (short SHA + subject), a one-line test summary, concerns, report path.
